I addressed all four iter-1 audit findings on the F003 event-messaging dispatch flow:

**Finding 3 (HIGH, correctness)** — Tightened breaker normalization in `event_copy.py:529` and `notify_event.py:268` to match exactly `breaker:patch_incomplete` (the only D009-authorized legacy colon-key), so `breaker:not_real` (and any other unknown breaker subtype) now falls through `DISPOSITION_TABLE.get()` and render returns `None` rather than synthesizing a fake `dontpanic approve p breaker:not_real` command.

**Finding 1 (HIGH, architectural)** — Threaded the `RenderedEvent` through dispatch sinks: `notify.notify_event(event, rendered=None)` and `notify_discord.notify(event, rendered=None)` (plus `_build_payload`) now accept the kwarg; `notify_event.dispatch_event` passes the RenderedEvent it already produced via `event_copy.render(event)` to both sinks so they no longer re-render — the load-bearing F003 contract is now actually wired. Legacy callers that omit the kwarg still get the in-sink fallback render.

**Finding 4 (MEDIUM, correctness)** — Documented in `event_copy.py` disposition table that `error` stays INBOX_ONLY because every `event="error"` emit site in supervisor.py writes only to INBOX (no `dispatch_event` call), so the render() path is unreachable; the `error` template stays as defensive coverage if a future emit site flips to LIVE/DASHBOARD_ACTION, citing D008.
